paragraphs: GIFT Nifty is at 24,442.5, down 37.5 points (-0.15%). The implied open for the cash Nifty is also 24,442.5, suggesting a gap down of about 94 points (-0.38%) from yesterday’s close of 24,536.6. The market may open lower, but the gap is historically sensitive to early buying.

US futures show mixed signals: S&P 500 futures are up 0.32% at 7,406.5, Nasdaq futures up 1.22% at 27,078.75, while Dow futures are down 0.53% at 51,343. Asian indices are broadly weaker – Nikkei down 5.27% at 57,858.6, Kospi down 3.96% at 5,170.42, Hang Seng down 0.31% at 24,721, Shanghai down 0.88% at 3,657.5, and Taiwan down 4.26% at 39,803.35. European markets closed modestly lower, with FTSE 100 down 0.43% at 10,782.66 and DAX down 0.43% at 26,325.0.

Commodities are mixed. Brent crude rose 1.66% to $99.92 and WTI to $91.67, lifting upstream oil stocks but adding cost pressure for OMCs, paints, airlines and tyres. Gold slipped 0.94% to 4,074.8 and silver 0.78% to 51.97, while copper is flat at 6.273 and natural gas up 1.80% at 3.0. The rupee held at 94.465 per dollar, the dollar index edged up 0.10% to 101.652, and US 10‑year yields fell 5.7 bps to 4.837, keeping financing costs modest.

Foreign investors have bought Rs 35,809 crore over the past five days, while domestic institutions sold Rs 19,045 crore. The options market shows a put‑call ratio of 1.39, indicating more puts than calls. Max‑pain sits at 24,350. ATM implied volatility is 15.95%.

A long list of earnings is slated for today, including 3MINDIA, AGIIL, HINDALCO, HMT, SIEMENS and VOLTAS among others. Macro events later today include US non‑farm payrolls (forecast 65 K), average hourly earnings (0.3%), and Canadian employment data. The US consumer sentiment and inflation expectations releases follow, while the BOJ governor will speak at 21:30 GMT.

At the same time, a GIFT Nifty drop of about 123 points keeps telecom, energy, consumer goods, metals and food stocks in focus. The AI‑related sell‑off in US tech adds a bearish tone to Indian IT, while higher crude prices favour upstream oil players.
